headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channel or write surface is documented, but Authelia’s broad egress could still amplify misrouting if paired with copied outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between authelia and awesome-nlp, and neither profile shows a default path for one to ingest the other’s outputs. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth, while awesome-nlp has no I/O surfaces. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies outputs from one agent into the other, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or queue is added later, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia is documented with broad network egress, but awesome-nlp has no documented I/O surfaces or data classes touched, and no shared workspace or credential principal is shown. With no evidence that sensitive data flows from one to the other, leakage is not established for this pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later mounted on the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF awesome-nlp is configured to ingest files or send context to a backend, reassess.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Run each agent under a separate OS account.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write or subprocess capability is listed; awesome-nlp has no write, network, or concurrency surface documented. Without overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no plausible capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or OAuth scope, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, reassess coordination.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can act as an authentication/ForwardAuth component, but awesome-nlp has no documented action-taking authority or verification pipeline. The pair does not show a default chain where one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, so cascading error is limited and mostly manual.
conditions: IF an operator uses awesome-nlp output as policy input to Authelia, errors can cascade.
IF Authelia decisions are automated from unverified text, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated text.
Use explicit validation rules for any text passed into Authelia.
requires-engineering: add schema checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either authelia or awesome-nlp. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced and the profiles do not show PHI or EU PII handling, no specific compliance mismatch can be substantiated.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, reassess residency and retention.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter policy than the other, compare controls.
mitigations: requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls if regulated data is introduced.
